stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$(K_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a system of perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ be the derived colimit
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-colimit}).
Then for any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom(K, E) = R\lim E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K_n^\vee
$$
where $(K_n^\vee)$ is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.
hypotheses: $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a ringed space; $(K_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ is a directed sequence of perfect objects in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, with homotopy colimit $K$; $E$ is any object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$.
conclusions: There is a canonical isomorphism $R\SheafHom(K,E)\simeq R\lim_n(E\otimes^\mathbf L_{\mathcal O_X}K_n^\vee)$, using the inverse system of perfect dual complexes.

reason: Uses biduality and distinguished triangles for sequential derived limits and colimits, identifying products of internal Homs with Hom out of sums.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $K$ and $E$ be objects
of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ with $E$ perfect. The diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
H^0(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} E^\vee) \times H^0(X, E)
\ar[r] \ar[d] &
H^0(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} E^\vee
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} E) \ar[d] \\
\Hom_X(E, K) \times H^0(X, E) \ar[r] &
H^0(X, K)
}
$$
commutes where the top horizontal arrow is the cup product, the
right vertical arrow uses
$\epsilon : E^\vee \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} E \to \mathcal{O}_X$
(Example \ref{example-dual-derived}), the left vertical arrow uses
Lemma \ref{lemma-dual-perfect-complex}, and the bottom horizontal
arrow is the obvious one.
hypotheses: $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a ringed space; $K,E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$; $E$ is perfect.
conclusions: The stated square relating cup product, the evaluation $E^\vee\otimes^\mathbf L E\to\mathcal O_X$, the identification $H^0(X,K\otimes^\mathbf L E^\vee)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,K)$, and evaluation of morphisms on global sections commutes.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $h : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Let $K, M$ be objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$. The
canonical map
$$
Lh^*R\SheafHom(K, M) \longrightarrow R\SheafHom(Lh^*K, Lh^*M)
$$
of Remark \ref{remark-prepare-fancy-base-change}
is an isomorphism in the following cases
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is perfect,
\item $h$ is flat, $K$ is pseudo-coherent, and $M$ is (locally) bounded below,
\item $\mathcal{O}_X$ has finite tor dimension over $h^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y$,
$K$ is pseudo-coherent, and $M$ is (locally) bounded below,
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $h:X\to Y$ is a morphism of ringed spaces, and $K,M\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$.

At least one alternative holds: (i) $K$ is perfect; (ii) $h$ is flat, $K$ is pseudo-coherent and $M$ is (locally) bounded below; or (iii) $\mathcal O_X$ has finite Tor dimension over $h^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$, $K$ is pseudo-coherent, and $M$ is (locally) bounded below.
conclusions: The canonical map $Lh^*R\SheafHom(K,M)\to R\SheafHom(Lh^*K,Lh^*M)$ is an isomorphism.

reason: Checks perfect-source case by strict-perfect representatives and constructs bounded-below refinements, but leaves substantial degree arguments omitted and appears to substitute M for L in the K-flat representative choice.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $K, M$ be objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $x \in X$. The canonical map
$$
R\SheafHom(K, M)_x \longrightarrow
R\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}}(K_x, M_x)
$$
is an isomorphism in the following cases
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is perfect,
\item $K$ is pseudo-coherent and $M$ is (locally) bounded below.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space, $K,M\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, and $x\in X$.
Either $K$ is perfect, or $K$ is pseudo-coherent and $M$ is (locally) bounded below.
conclusions: The canonical stalk map $R\SheafHom(K,M)_x\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(K_x,M_x)$ is an isomorphism.

reason: Applies flat base change of derived internal Hom to the singleton ringed space at a stalk.
